What's covered by the exemption
Gold/silver bullion, leaf, foil, and similar items
How they decide what counts as bullion
The state asks whether the item is priced for its metal value (qualifying bullion) or for rarity, design, or collector demand (taxable).
What's NOT covered
Jewelry, rarity-priced collectibles, paper currency held as collectible, fabricated/industrial-use precious metal, and accessories.
Even when the state-level rule is clear, cities or counties in this state may charge their own tax. Here's what to expect.
Local treatment

Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in North Carolina.
Is gold and silver bullion taxable in North Carolina?
+
No. North Carolina fully exempts gold/silver bullion, leaf, foil, and similar items when value is based on metal content.
What determines whether an item qualifies as exempt bullion in North Carolina?
+
The key test is whether the item’s value is based on metal content rather than design or form.
Are numismatic (collector) coins exempt in North Carolina?
+
It depends. Numismatic treatment is conditional, and items sold primarily for collector premium may be taxable.
Is precious-metal jewelry taxed in North Carolina?
+
Yes. Jewelry is taxable, and state plus applicable local sales taxes can apply.
